title: Going to New York and working with Sharkey at Nick's
summary: In 1936 he went to New York, worked clubs, then Sharkey got him to join at Nick's; he made a Warner short but not Sharkey's records.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, with his afternoon sessions, drink beer, and a whole crowd of saxophone players, just to see how it sounds. And well it went on like that. The fellas different jobs working around. And then in 1936 I went to New York, just on my own, and just decided to go and see what it was. And I worked around different clubs in New York, you know. And then Sharky came up there right after. I was working on a job in Brooklyn, and he begged me to come to work with him at Knicks. And incidentally we had this Henry Adler who is quite a famous teacher now, drums and drum teacher in New York. He played with us in Knicks. And George Ebrunas played trombone. And I made a movie short for Warner Brothers. It was the first time I think I ever recorded, was on this movie short.
Had you planned to make records with Sharky?
Well, some funny thing happened that Sharky made quite a few records, but he never did use me. And I was on the same job with him.
That's funny. I think he was using Joe Marcella.
